MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, NOVEMBER 3, 2021

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:
The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Planning
Commission meeting on Wednesday, November 3, 2021, in the Council
Chambers, on the ninth floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge
of Allegiance by Commissioner Patricia Patrick, the meeting was
called to order at 7:00 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:
Present: Acting Chairwoman Commissioner Aide Trejo
  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Cheryl Shaw-Williams
Excused
Absence: Chairman Larry Springs

Staff:  Christopher E. Jackson, Sr., ECD Director
  Mindy Wilcox, AICP, Planning Manager
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner
  Jeff Lewis, Assistant City Attorney
  Arturo Salazar, Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Planner
  Angel Leon-Martell, Assistant Planner
  Christine Rivera, Assistant Planner
  Sean May, Planning Technician
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary
  Via Community Phone Call Coverage:
  AT&T Conference Call Operator Rep.

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:
Ms. Wilcox, Planning Manager stated Chairman Larry Springs called
out for an Excused Absence and introduced Christine Rivera, new
Assistant Planner.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
None (Confirmed by AT&T Operator).

(5) MINUTES:
Acting Chairwoman Trejo called for Minutes approval for April 13,
2020 Planning Commission meeting, was approved and the motion was
carried with –

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Shaw-Williams, and Acting
  Chairwoman Trejo.

(6) PUBLIC HEARINGS:

6A. ZONING CODE AMENDMENT NO. 2020-001 (ZCA-2020-001) CHAPTER 12
IMC:A continued public hearing to consider actions associated with
the Draft Westchester/Veterans and Crenshaw/Imperial Transit
Oriented Development Plans (TOD Plans) and Design Guidelines
including the following:
a. Environmental Impact Report EA-EIR-2021-066 (EA-EIR-2021-066)
  to assess the proposed TOD plans effects to the environment
  and community; and
b. General Plan Amend No. 2021-001 (GPA-2021-001) to modify the
  Land Use and Circulation Elements of the Inglewood General Plan
  for the TOD Plans; and
c. Zone Change No. 2021-001 (ZC-2021-001) to establish Zoning
  Designations contained within the TOD Plans; and
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
November 3, 2021
d.  Zoning Code Amendment No. 2021-004 (ZCA-2021-004) to Chapter
  12 of the Inglewood Municipal Code to establish regulations
  for the TOD Plans; and
e.  Establish Design Guidelines (DG-2021-001) for the TOD Plans.

Mr. Christopher E. Jackson, Sr. ECD Director, made a short
presentation with video backup to address questions that were asked
by the community at the Special Planning Commission Meeting in
August, 2021.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Senior Planner, made the staff presentation.

Acting Chairwoman Trejo asked the Planning Commission if there
were any questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick asked staff –
 Will this affect SB9 which was passed in September 2021?
   Ms. Wilcox stated it won’t change anything that was placed in
  the TOD Plan, but City of Inglewood will follow what is
  required by the State of California.

Commissioner Rice asked staff about the Property Based Improvement
District?
   Ms. Wilcox stated that funds obtained from property owners
  and business owners to cover shared costs like street cleaning
  and advertising of commercial districts.
   Mr. Jackson stated that this is just a suggestion at this
  point and has not been implemented into the TOD Plan. There
  are specific state statutes that must be followed and this
  sets in motion the discussion so that staff can begin to talk
  about how the City will handle some of the more intensive
  commercial areas.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked staff –
 What is the proposed Inglewood Transit Connector and what will
  that do regarding people who will be riding metro?
   Ms. Wilcox stated that Inglewood Transit Connector is a
  proposed train line, proposed by the City, separate from this
  project. It is proposed to connect the downtown metro station
  all the way to the right-of-way area adjacent to the new So-
  Fi Stadium.

Acting Chairwoman Trejo stated:
 She also had the same question as Commissioner Patrick with
  regards to SB9 and how the State of California has impacted the
  City. How there are now Accessory Dwelling Units being built
  all over the state and she stated her question would be with
  regards to parking in the City, because of the greater impact
  of multiple vehicles per each current home and now there will
  be added vehicles with the addition of the ADU’s.

Acting Chairwoman Trejo opened the public hearing and opened up
the phone lines from the AT&T operator to hear from the public to
speak “For or Against” this item.

FOR / AGAINST:
Mr. Joe Buke of Liberator for the Southwest Regional Council of
Contractors and Local Area Chapter, gave a statement on Item 6A
and the effects of the EIR and how traffic will impact the City if
Inglewood does not require local workforce hire.

Acting Chairwoman Trejo closed the public hearing, and thanked
staff for a wonderful job in their presentation to the public both
in September at the various Council member town-hall meetings and
  2
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
November 3, 2021
in addressing all issues felt by the local communities, which was
likely due to misunderstanding and unfounded confusion, but staff
has done an excellent job at making sure the public and the
community have been made aware of the truth.

Acting Chairwoman Trejo asked for final comments from the Planning
Commissioners, there were none, and asked for a motion from the
Planning Commission.

MOTION:
The motion was made by Commissioner Shaw-Williams to adopt a
resolution recommending that the City Council certify the Draft
Final Environmental Impact Report EA-EIR-2021-066, adopt a
resolution recommending City Council adoption of General Plan
Amendment GPA-2021-001, adopt a resolution recommending City
Council adoption of Zoning Code Amendment ZCA-2021-004 and Zone
Change ZC-2021-001, and adopt a resolution recommending the City
Council adoption of the Westchester/Veterans and Crenshaw
/Imperial TOD Plans and Design Guidelines DG-2021-001; Resolutions
1906 thru 1909;

Be approved.

The motion was carried with –

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Shaw-Williams, and Acting
  Chairwoman Trejo.

There is no appeal process per Ms. Wilcox. This item will
continue to the City Council for their consideration.

6B. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2021-009 (SP-2021-009) 336 EAST
HILLCREST BOULEVARD: A public hearing to consider an application
by Brian Massie, representing the Owner, for Special Use Permit
No. 2021-009 (SP-2021-009) to allow: 1) The sale of beer, wine,
and  distilled  spirits  for  on-site  consumption;  2)  Live
entertainment; and 3) Alternative modes of transportation for an
outdoor event space located on the rooftop of an existing six-
story, mixed-use building on an approximately 23,200 square-foot,
H-C (TOD-Historic Core) zoned property at 336 East Hillcrest
Boulevard.

Ms. Marissa Fewell, Planner, made the staff presentation.

Acting Chairwoman Trejo asked the Planning Commission if there
were any questions for staff.

Acting Chairwoman asked staff – questions regarding the rooftop
use, amenities for the residents, who controls and identifies
special event participants?
-  Ms. Fewell answered Acting Chairwoman’s questions.

Commissioner Rice asked staff – questions regarding the special
events use by the applicant, such as maximum occupancy, required
parking spaces designated for the special events.
-  Both Ms. Fewell and Ms. Wilcox answered Commissioner Rice’s
  questions.

Commissioner Patrick made a comment to staff regarding any parking
studies on the proposed parking lifts that the applicant will be
utilizing, along with any liability at the site for using the
lifts.

Acting Chairwoman Trejo asked the applicant to come forward to
address the Planning Commission and speak about his project.
  3
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
November 3, 2021

Mr. Pete Mozel, Architect for the applicant addressed the planning
commission regarding the parking, and occupants for the rooftop
events, as well as how the building will be able to be utilized by
the community during the daytime and afternoons, with the rooftop
service being utilized during the late afternoon and evenings in
conjunction to events occurring at the So-Fi Stadium.

Acting Chairwoman Trejo asked the Planning Commission if they had
any questions for the applicant.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked the applicant several questions
regarding the vehicle lifts and other businesses in the area who
might want to utilize this current lift, especially for the valet
use.
-  Mr. Mozel answered Commissioner Shaw-Williams’ questions.

Commissioner Rice asked the applicant regarding the rooftop events
that might have any effects on the residents in the community
surrounding the location.
-  Mr. Mozel answered Commissioner Rice’s question.

Acting Chairwoman Trejo asked the applicant about receiving any
noise complaints from the surrounding community, would there be a
24 hour contact person in order to reduce the music levels if too
loud.
-  Mr. Mozel answered Acting Chairwoman Trejo’s question.

Commissioner Rice asked additional questions regarding times of
operation and the layout of the top floor, and utilizing potted
plants as a buffer of the music volume.
-  Mr. Mozel and Mr. Brian Napp (Under-development Manager) of
  the project replied to Commissioner Rice’s question.

Acting Chairwoman Trejo asked the applicants one more question
regarding any Super Bowl events or any major celebratory events,
and for the applicant to do community outreach.
-  Mr. Napp answered Commissioner Trejo’s question.

Acting Chairwoman Trejo wanted to open the public hearing and open
up the phone lines from the AT&T operator to hear from the public
to speak “For or Against” this item.

FOR / AGAINST:
None, confirmed by the AT&T Operator.

Acting Chairwoman Trejo closed the public hearing, and asked for
final comments from the Planning Commissioners, there were none,
and asked for a motion from the Planning Commission.

MOTION:
The motion was made by Commissioner Rice to affirm the categorical
exemption EA-CE-2021-090, and to adopt the attached resolution
approving SP-2021-009, subject to the 24 conditions plus two (2)
additional conditions along with a 6 month and an 18 month review,
before the Planning Commission and was seconded by Commissioner
Shaw-Williams, Resolution No. 1910

6C. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2021-010 (SP-2021-010) 3111 WEST CENTURY
BOULEVARD: A public hearing to consider an application by Hao Shen,
representing the Owner, for Special Use Permit No. 2021-010 (SP-
2021-010) to allow a hair salon within 300 feet of a similar use,
on an approximately 30,940 square-foot, C-2(General Commercial)
zoned property at 3111 West Century Boulevard.

Mr. Angel Leon-Martell,  Assistant  Planner,  made  the  staff
presentation.

Acting Chairwoman Trejo asked the Planning Commission if there
were any questions for staff, there were none, she asked the
applicant to come forward to address the Planning Commission and
speak about her project.

Ms. Betty Yao, representative for the applicant to address the
planning commission.

Commissioner Patrick asked the applicant regarding any parking
issues at the site.
-  Ms. Yao answered Commissioner Patrick’s question.

Acting Chairwoman Trejo opened the public hearing to the audience
to speak either for or against this project.

FOR: / AGAINST:
None, (Confirmed by the AT&T Operator).

Acting Chairwoman Trejo closed the public hearing and asked for
any final comments from the Planning Commissioners. There were
none, and called for a motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner Patrick motioned to affirm the categorical exemption
EA-CE-2021-090 and adopt the attached resolution approving SP-
2021-010, subject to the 12 conditions and was seconded by
Commissioner Shaw-Williams, Resolution No. 1911

November 3, 2021
  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING A
  SPECIAL USE PERMIT TO HAO SHEN, REPRESENTING
  DAVID KHEDR, TO ALLOW A HAIR SALON, WITHIN 300

  ZONED PROPERTY AT 3111 WEST CENTURY BOULEVARD.

Be approved.

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Shaw-Williams and Acting

Ms. Wilcox explained the appeal process.

6D. SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2021-011 (SP-2021-011) 2218 WEST 79TH
STREET: A public hearing to consider an application by Tallulah
Marcelin, representing the Owner, for Special Use Permit No. 2021-
011 (SP-2021-011) to allow a hair salon within 300 feet of a
similar use, on an approximately 7,878 square-foot, C-2(General
Commercial) zoned property at 2218 West 79th Street.

Mr. Arturo Salazar, Planner, made the staff presentation.

Acting Chairwoman Trejo asked the Planning Commission if there
were any questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick asked staff about the exact location of the
proposed site.
-  Mr. Salazar answered Commissioner Patrick’s question.

Commissioner Rice asked staff for clarification and location of
the other hair salons within the area.
-  Mr. Salazar answered Commissioner Rice’s question.

Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked staff about any permit parking
program for the area.
-  Mr. Salazar answered Commissioner Shaw-Williams’ question.

Acting Chairwoman Trejo made a statement about making Security
Cameras a condition of approval and asked staff regarding
lighting at the site and in the area, along with how dark is the
site during the evenings.
-  Mr. Salazar answered Chairwoman Trejo’s questions.

Commissioner Rice asked staff if the building is commercial.
-  Mr. Salazar answered Commissioner Rice’s question.

Acting Chairwoman Trejo asked the applicant to come forward twice
to address the Planning Commission and speak about her project.

No response from the applicant, (Confirmed by the AT&T Operator).

Acting Chairwoman Trejo opened the public hearing to the audience
to speak either for or against this project.

FOR: / AGAINST:
None, (Confirmed by the AT&T Operator).

Acting Chairwoman Trejo closed the public hearing and asked for
any final comments from the Planning Commissioners. There were
none, and called for a motion.

  6
 Inglewood Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
November 3, 2021
Assistant Attorney Lewis stated to the Planning Commission, if
there is the possibility that there may be a Deny-vote for this
item, due to the location being within 300 feet or the fact that
the applicant was not present for this meeting, he requests the
planning commission offer a continuance on behalf of the
applicant in order for them to have an opportunity to present
their project.

Acting Chairwoman Trejo stated that she understood and asked for
a motion of continuance from the Planning Commission.

MOTION:
Commissioner Shaw-Williams asked for a motion of continuance to
the next scheduled Planning Commission meeting of December 1, 2021
to allow the applicant an opportunity to come before the Planning
Commission and was seconded by Commissioner Rice.

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Shaw-Williams and Acting
  Chairwoman Trejo.

(7)  NON - PUBLIC HEARINGS:

7A. DESIGN REVIEW NO. 2021-006 (DR-2021-006) 132 SOUTH MARKET
STREET:  A non-public hearing to consider an application by Andy
Fiscella, representing The Dime, for Design Review No. 2021-006
(DR-2021-006) to approve exterior and interior alterations to an
existing 3,500 square-foot two-story commercial building on an
approximately 4,625 square-foot, H-C (TOD Historic Core) zoned
property at 132 South Market Street.

Mr. Arturo Salazar, Planner, made the staff presentation.

Acting Chairwoman Trejo asked the Planning Commission if there
were any questions for staff, there were none, and called for a
motion.

MOTION:
Commissioner  Shaw-Williams  motioned  to  affirm  categorical
exemption EA-CE-2021-097 and adopt the attached resolution
approving DR-2021-006 subject to the 8 conditions and was seconded
by Commissioner Patrick.

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Shaw-Williams and Acting
  Chairwoman Trejo.

Ms. Mindy Wilcox explained the appeal process.

(8) PUBLIC COMMENTS:
Ms. Patricia Smith, Inglewood Resident in District No. 4 asked
if the City will be utilizing Eminent Domain for the TOD Plan for
the Westchester/Veterans and Crenshaw/Imperial project, since she
is a homeowner in the Crenshaw/Imperial zone.
-  Mr. Jackson replied the answer to Ms. Smith.

 Revitalization of the City of Inglewood is all fine and well,

  have a Happy Thanksgiving.

Commissioner Rice -
